newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Long basket deals feature on Hungary FX futures.
newsitem.headline: Long basket deals feature on Hungary FX futures.

text.p: The opening of a new March 1998 contract for the dollar triggered a spate of long-term mark/dollar basket deals on the Budapest currency futures market as dealers anticipated a fall in short-term yields, traders said on Friday.

March sales of marks and dollars in proportion to their 70/30 percent proportion in the central bank's currency basket accounted for two-thirds of moderate turnover of 5.25 billion forints on the Budapest Commodity Exchange's financial futures market.
"Many people think short yields will go down in the next few weeks so they are making basket deals as far ahead as they can," said Mihaly Eotvos of OTP Forex.
Basket deals are seen as a means of hedging against large fluctuations in the dollar/mark crosses.
Under the central bank's crawling peg devaluation system, the forint is devalued by 1.1 percent per month against a currency basket made uo 70 percent of the mark and 30 percent of the dollar.
The new March 1998 maturity for the dollar opened at 201 forints while the March mark was steady at 120 forints.
The Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) forex futures market was tradeless.
Central bank spot rates for the mark and dollar were fixed at midday at 104.77 forints to the mark, down 0.05, and 180.26 to the dollar, up 0.42.
